title: Concepts, categories and rational models of categorisation
summary: Concepts and categories and their functions; the classical and statistical views; two-class classification with parametric class models; prototype effects (Posner and Keele) and their model; the limits of classification as a model of concepts; exemplar models and neural networks; unsupervised and semi-supervised learning; mixture models and unknown numbers of categories.

objectives.description: Objectives for this unit will be finalised when it is prepared; the source material is OCW lecture 12 (concepts and categories; statistical pattern recognition; Posner and Keele; limitations), lectures 14–16 (unsupervised and semi-supervised learning; exemplar models and neural networks) and the web book's Mixture models chapter.

preparation.description: Read OCW lecture 12 slides 30–52 (concepts and categories; statistical pattern recognition; the parametric Gaussian approach and its learning; relevance to human concept learning; Posner and Keele; limitations).
Read OCW lectures 14 (unsupervised and semi-supervised learning), 15 and 16 (non-parametric classification: exemplar models and neural networks).
Read the web book's Mixture models chapter (learning categories; categorical perception of speech sounds; unknown numbers of categories). Reference-only.
